summary.en: Follow the iterator protocol, build lazy sequences with yield and recognize one-pass consumption.
summary.bn: ইটারেটর দিয়ে একবারে একটি মান নাও, yield দিয়ে জেনারেটর বানাও এবং পড়ে ফেলা মান আবার আসে না কেন বোঝো।

notes: Python 3.10–3.12 use the same iterator protocol and modern generator StopIteration rule. Async iteration and bidirectional generator methods are outside this lesson.

sections.title: Ask for the next value when you need it
Translate a for loop into protocol steps
Separate creation time from request time
Plan one pass and bound infinite work
Compare two passes with one shared cursor
Treat a generator as a suspended one-pass computation

examples.title: Implement a countdown iterator
examples.explanationHtml: The first next consumes 3. The list consumes 2 and 1, after which the supplied default reports exhaustion.

examples.title: Pause a yielding squares function
examples.explanationHtml: The first request yields zero. The remaining request consumes 1, 4 and 9; the next traversal is empty because the same generator is exhausted.

examples.title: Observe delayed execution
examples.explanationHtml: Creating the generator prints nothing from its body. The first request prints start, and the second resumes the body and prints resume.

examples.title: Filter and sum without a result list
examples.explanationHtml: The generator supplies 40, 75 and 90 to sum for a total of 205. sum exhausts it, so the subsequent list is empty.

examples.title: Bound an endless source
examples.explanationHtml: islice consumes only the first four multiples. The generator then continues at 15 rather than restarting at three.

practice.title: Yield even values up to a limit
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 100. Write evens(n) yielding even integers from zero through n inclusive. Print them separated by spaces.
hints: The inclusive upper boundary needs n + 1.

practice.title: Build a running total generator
practice.statementHtml: Read one line of integers, possibly empty. Yield the cumulative total after each value. Print those totals on one line; an empty input gives an empty line.

practice.title: Consume only a prefix
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20. Build an infinite generator of positive squares and use islice to take n. Print their sum.
hints: Bound the consumer, not the unbounded source.

practice.title: Make a stepped iterator
practice.statementHtml: Read start stop step, integers between -100 and 100 with step positive. Define a Stepper iterator yielding start, start+step and so on while below stop. Print its values then END on a separate line.
hints: Update position before returning each value.

practice.title: Find the first passing mark lazily
practice.statementHtml: Read one line of marks from 0 to 100, possibly empty. Write a generator yielding only marks at least 40. Use next with a default to print the first passing mark or NONE when no mark passes.
hints: The consumer needs one result, so it need not exhaust the source.

quiz.prompt: What remains after requesting one square?
quiz.explanation: next consumes the first value before list consumes the rest.

quiz.prompt: When does a generator body first print?
quiz.explanation: The body starts on the first request.

quiz.prompt: What does next with a default return after exhaustion?
quiz.explanation: The default is returned instead of raising on exhaustion.
An iterator supports the iterable protocol by returning itself.

quiz.prompt: How should a generator function end normally?
quiz.explanation: Escaping StopIteration inside a generator becomes RuntimeError.
Parenthesized comprehension syntax creates a generator expression.

quiz.prompt: Does lazy evaluation guarantee less total computation?
quiz.explanation: It can avoid unused work and result storage, but consumed values still need computation.

quiz.prompt: What happens when two names reference one generator?
quiz.explanation: Assignment aliases the same suspended computation.

quiz.prompt: Why is list(count()) unsuitable for a finite report?
options: The source has no normal end
quiz.explanation: Use a finite bound such as islice.

quiz.prompt: Where can a conversion inside a generator raise?
options: Only when the generator object is created
quiz.explanation: The generator body runs when requested.

quiz.prompt: When is a list usually more suitable than a generator?
options: When repeated traversal and indexing are required
quiz.explanation: A finite stored sequence supports reuse and indexing directly.

keyPoints.en: iter obtains an iterator and next requests its next value.
keyPoints.bn: iter দিয়ে ইটারেটর পাও আর next দিয়ে পরের মান চাও।
আর মান না থাকলে StopIteration দিয়ে ইটারেটর শেষ হওয়ার খবর দেয়।

keyPoints.en: Calling a generator function creates a suspended generator.
keyPoints.bn: জেনারেটর ফাংশন কল করলে সঙ্গে সঙ্গে বডি চলে না, জেনারেটর অবজেক্ট তৈরি হয়।

keyPoints.en: yield produces one value and preserves local state.
keyPoints.bn: yield একটি মান দেয় আর পরে চালানোর জন্য লোকাল অবস্থা ধরে রাখে।

keyPoints.en: Generator expressions compute values on demand.
keyPoints.bn: জেনারেটর এক্সপ্রেশন দরকার হলে একেকটি মান হিসাব করে।

keyPoints.en: Lazy processing can save memory without reducing total work.
keyPoints.bn: লেজি প্রসেসিংয়ে মেমরি বাঁচতে পারে, তবে মোট হিসাবের কাজ কমবেই এমন নয়।

examQuestions.question: Distinguish an iterable from an iterator.
examQuestions.answerHtml: An iterable can supply an iterator through iter. An iterator tracks one traversal, returns itself from __iter__, and supplies values through __next__ until StopIteration. A list can provide independent iterators; one generator normally represents one pass.

examQuestions.question: Explain lazy memory use and one limitation of a generator pipeline.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A pipeline can pass one value at a time without a full result list, reducing result storage. It still holds suspended local state and source references, and consuming every item still performs every required calculation. A second traversal needs a fresh generator or stored values.

examQuestions.question: Describe a running-total generator and its behavior on empty input.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Initialize total to zero. For each value, add it and yield total. The local total survives between requests. Empty input reaches the end without yielding, so list of the generator is empty and a print of its expanded values produces an empty line.

def running(values):
    total = 0
    for value in values:
        total += value
        yield total

list(running([2, -1, 5])) is [2, 1, 6]. list(running([])) is empty.
